candidates.exact_span: 4Q3             Lowest four-day average flow rate expected to occur once every three-years
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 4Q3 flow statistic may govern flow-dependent effluent limits (Purpose A) or flow-conditioned monitoring triggers and frequencies (Purpose B); different interpretations of what flow value qualifies as 4Q3 would change which limit or monitoring obligation applies.

Whether a requirement is a BMP (non-numeric management plan) versus an enforceable numeric effluent limit affects Purpose A limit applicability comparisons and Purpose B monitoring-obligation classification; interpreting BMP as a plan versus practices/measure could change whether numeric compliance analysis is performed.

candidates.exact_span: BOD             Biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: The five-day qualifier and 'unless noted otherwise' condition determine which BOD limit variant applies to a reported measurement; misinterpreting the applicable BOD form would pair measurements with the wrong numeric limit in Purpose A.

candidates.exact_span: CBOD            Carbonaceous biochemical oxygen demand (five-day unless noted otherwise)
candidates.computation_change_reason: CBOD is distinct from total BOD; interpreting a reported or limited parameter as CBOD versus BOD (or applying the five-day default incorrectly) would change which enforceable numeric limit is selected for comparison in Purpose A.

Critical dilution is used in deriving or applying dilution-dependent effluent limits; a different interpretation of the CD value or its role would change the computed applicable numeric limit under Purpose A.

DMRs are the primary evidence of performed monitoring and reported results; what counts as a DMR submission or its contents affects whether monitoring was required and performed (Purpose B) and how missing or non-numeric results are classified (Purpose C).

Limits cited as ELG-based derive from federal effluent guidelines; interpreting whether a parameter limit is ELG-sourced versus another basis changes which enforceable numeric limit applies in Purpose A.

Method minimum level governs whether a reported value is usable for numeric compliance comparison (Purpose A) and whether a result should be treated as below detection, non-detect, or missing evidence (Purpose C); conflating ML with MQL would change both computations.

Minimum quantification level determines when a numeric result is considered quantified for limit comparison (Purpose A) versus treated as unquantified or missing (Purpose C); different interpretations of MQL versus ML would change exceedance findings and missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: NMWQS           New Mexico State Standards for Interstate and Intrastate Surface Waters
candidates.computation_change_reason: Limits grounded in NMWQS may differ from permit-specific or technology-based limits; interpreting a limit as NMWQS-based versus another source changes the applicable numeric standard evaluated in Purpose A.

BPJ-derived limits are set by permit writer judgment rather than fixed tables; interpreting whether a limit is BPJ-based affects which numeric value is treated as enforceable and whether alternative derivation methods apply in Purpose A.

Reasonable-potential findings can trigger stricter effluent limits (Purpose A) and additional or more frequent monitoring requirements (Purpose B); different interpretations of whether RP has been established would change applicable limits and monitoring obligations.
TMDL-based allocations can establish or modify effluent limits; interpreting whether a limit is TMDL-derived changes the numeric limit selected for compliance comparison in Purpose A.

WET requirements use pass/fail toxicity endpoints rather than ordinary numeric concentration limits and carry distinct monitoring schedules; misclassifying a WET requirement as a standard numeric limit (or vice versa) would change Purpose A comparisons and Purpose B monitoring-applicability determinations.

Wasteload allocations translate water-quality targets into facility-specific limits; different interpretations of WLA values or their binding effect would change the enforceable numeric limit applied in Purpose A.
pH limits are expressed in standard units rather than mg/l; misinterpreting the unit basis for pH measurements would cause incorrect numeric limit pairing and exceedance determination in Purpose A.
